blocking.section: Runbooks > Ruralz Control rebuild from Git (step 7); Runbooks > Holding deliveries during recovery (paragraph after step 4); RPO and RTO (rows 'Control Store and every backup lost' and 'Re-enrollment of every Node'); Game days GD-10
blocking.issue: Partly resolved. The revision now describes the collapse of the published Node count after a rebuild, or after a restore without a revocation list, and adds OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 (blocking for M2). Three problems remain. (1) The runbooks still have no step for it. The only mitigation is a sentence saying 'declared ceilings avoid it', and during recovery an operator cannot declare ceilings, because the hold forbids digest changes ('aligning needs a delivery'). (2) Three claims in the same document still say traffic is unchanged. Rebuild step 7 says traffic changes only by the draining zone's capacity. The rebuild row's traffic RTO is 'As above', which resolves to 'Zero request errors (target)'. The Re-enrollment row's traffic RTO is 'One zone's capacity drains at a time (target)'. All three contradict the collapse paragraph. (3) Under the current option (c) of OQ-9, GD-10 cannot pass its own criterion, and the document does not say that GD-10 requires option (a). Failure scenario: a 3,000-Node Cell uses derived ceilings and has a hot key at 20% of one shard. Every backup is lost. The zone-a re-enrollment wave brings 1,000 Nodes online on the rebuilt deployment. They have fresh `node.id`s and are unqualified, so their first `HeartbeatReply` carries a near-zero count. Each of those Nodes derives a ceiling of about 2 × `requests`, and hot-key GCRA calls rise from about 2 × `requests` toward 1,000 × 2 × `requests` per window. The shard's State client breakers open, so co-tenant Rate Limits fall back to local buckets and `closed` Token Budgets return `RZ-STS-003`. That is a request error the RTO row says cannot happen. The count then needs about 58 minutes (hypothesis) to recover, and each later zone wave repeats the collapse.
blocking.evidence: Rebuild step 7: "Re-enroll Cluster by Cluster, one zone at a time ... Traffic changes only by the draining zone's capacity (target)." Holding deliveries: "After a rebuild, or a restore without a revocation list, no Node is qualified, so the first `HeartbeatReply` can collapse the published count until OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 decides; [declared ceilings] avoid it". RPO and RTO: "| Control Store and every backup lost | ... | As above | 8 hours or less ..." where the row above reads "Zero request errors (target); Node count per the [hold]"; "| Re-enrollment of every Node | Enrollment identities | None (target) | One zone's capacity drains at a time (target) |". GD-10: "the published count drops at most 10% (target); no State client breaker opens". Hold step 2: "(no digest changes)"; step 3: "aligning needs a delivery". Scalability and distributed state, Ruralz Control availability: "a near-zero count sends derived ceilings to the full limit, multiplying hot-key GCRA calls. Only qualified Nodes, keyed by `node.id` in committed state ... may lower it".
blocking.fix: (1) Add a numbered hold step 0 that runs before any Node connects or re-enrolls: 'For each Cluster whose served Revision uses derived ceilings, until OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 (a) ships: confirm that hot keys above 25% of a shard are `localOnly` in the served Revision. Otherwise, before re-enrolling, shift the Cell's weight to other Cells, or accept the bound below and watch State client breakers.' (2) Add a readiness rule to Local rate-limit fallback or Backups: 'Control-mode Clusters that depend on a rebuild or a list-less restore SHOULD declare per-Node ceilings in advance, because recovery cannot deliver them.' (3) Qualify rebuild step 7 and the 'Control Store and every backup lost' and 'Re-enrollment of every Node' traffic RTO cells: 'plus, with derived ceilings, up to N_reenrolled × 2 × `requests` per key per window and possible shard breaker opening until the count re-qualifies, about 58 minutes (hypothesis), unless OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 (a)'. Remove 'Zero request errors (target)' from the rebuild row, or make it conditional on declared ceilings or OQ-9 (a). (4) In GD-10, add the precondition 'with OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 (a) implemented, or with declared ceilings'. Also add a variant that uses derived ceilings and asserts the stated over-admission bound.

non_blocking.section: RPO and RTO (row 'Node lost'); Game days GD-1
non_blocking.suggestion: Pod release on Kubernetes is not automatic for StatefulSet pods on an unreachable host (T4). Under the current option (b) of OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-2, the '5 minutes' is an on-call response target. Say so ('release by force-delete or out-of-service taint, paged, within 5 minutes (target)'), and have the GD-1 host variant measure detection plus release, not only the 30 s after release.

non_blocking.section: Backups > Taking and checking backups (rules 1 and 5); RPO and RTO
non_blocking.suggestion: Rule 1 tags the 10-minute copy '(hypothesis)', but the RPO row tags the same figure '(target)'; use one tag. With hourly backups and a copy within 10 minutes, the newest copy is normally at most 70 minutes old. An alert at 75 minutes therefore fires only once the RPO is breached. Consider alerting at 70 minutes (target) so on-call gets warning before the breach.

Capacity planning bounds the reconnect storm as λ_storm × (c_hs + c_up) ≤ 10% of survivor CPU (target), but step 2 writes only λ_storm × c_hs. Either include c_up or say why the upgrade GCRA term is zero for a regional move.

Step 1 runs non-home step 5, which reverts empty-plan Rollouts with `ruralz rollout start`. That needs a working Ruralz Control, which is lost in this scenario. Say that step 5 applies only after the restore, or only to Regions served by the restored deployment.

The re-enrollment formula line is tagged (hypothesis), but its parameter legend is tagged (target). Tag the legend values (t_drain about 30 s from ZG-4, the 30 to 60 s slow start) individually, so it is clear which inputs are objectives and which are estimates.
